atoms.text: This guide configures the FlowGate load balancer to deliver access logs to a bucket named lb-access-logs. The bucket and the delivery role, flowgate-log-writer, both belong to account 111122223333. Create the role with a trust policy that allows the FlowGate service principal to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows PutObject on arn:objstore:::lb-access-logs/flowgate/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:objstore:::lb-access-logs. Do not modify the bucket policy, because the same-account identity-based policy is the only source of the grant. Enable log delivery on the load balancer with a five-minute interval and the prefix flowgate/. After the first interval, confirm that gzip-compressed objects named by date and load balancer ID appear under the prefix. If delivery fails, compare the resource ARNs in the role policy against the bucket name and prefix.

This guide configures the FlowGate load balancer to deliver access logs to a bucket named lb-access-logs. The bucket belongs to account 444455556666, while the delivery role, flowgate-log-writer, belongs to account 111122223333. Create the role in account 111122223333 with a trust policy that allows the FlowGate service principal to assume it. The bucket owner then adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:iam::111122223333:role/flowgate-log-writer as the principal and allows PutObject on arn:objstore:::lb-access-logs/flowgate/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:objstore:::lb-access-logs. The bucket policy in the owning account is the source of the grant, so nothing about the role's own account permissions is relied on. Enable log delivery on the load balancer with a five-minute interval and the prefix flowgate/. After the first interval, confirm that gzip-compressed objects named by date and load balancer ID appear under the prefix. If delivery fails, compare the principal and resource ARNs in the bucket policy against the role ARN, bucket name, and prefix.

This guide sets up TrailKeeper to write account audit events to a bucket named audit-trail-archive. The bucket and the TrailKeeper delivery role, trailkeeper-writer, are both in account 111122223333. Create the role with a trust policy for the TrailKeeper service principal. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on arn:objstore:::audit-trail-archive/trails/111122223333/* and GetBucketAcl on arn:objstore:::audit-trail-archive. Leave the bucket policy unchanged, since the role's identity-based policy alone grants the access within the same account. Create a trail that writes JSON event files every five minutes to the trails/ prefix. Verify delivery by listing the prefix and checking that each file contains events with timestamps from the last interval. A missing file usually indicates a typo in the resource ARN of the role policy.

This guide sets up TrailKeeper to write account audit events to a bucket named audit-trail-archive. The bucket is in account 444455556666, and the TrailKeeper delivery role, trailkeeper-writer, is in account 111122223333. Create the role in account 111122223333 with a trust policy for the TrailKeeper service principal. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming account 111122223333 as the principal that allows PutObject on arn:objstore:::audit-trail-archive/trails/111122223333/* and GetBucketAcl on arn:objstore:::audit-trail-archive. That statement in the bucket policy carries the grant across the account boundary. Create a trail that writes JSON event files every five minutes to the trails/ prefix. Verify delivery by listing the prefix and checking that each file contains events with timestamps from the last interval. A missing file usually indicates a wrong account ID or resource ARN in the bucket policy statement.

This guide configures EdgeRelay to export CDN request logs to a bucket named edge-request-logs. The bucket and the export role, edgerelay-exporter, belong to account 111122223333. Create the role with a trust policy that lets the EdgeRelay service principal assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on arn:objstore:::edge-request-logs/cdn/*, because large hourly files are uploaded in parts. The bucket policy remains as it is, and the identity-based policy is the only grant. In the EdgeRelay distribution settings, select the role, set the prefix to cdn/, and choose hourly partitioning by date. Wait for the next hour boundary and check that a directory named for the date and hour contains tab-separated log files. Incomplete uploads that remain visible in the bucket indicate that AbortMultipartUpload is missing from the policy.

This guide configures EdgeRelay to export CDN request logs to a bucket named edge-request-logs. The bucket belongs to account 444455556666, and the export role, edgerelay-exporter, belongs to account 111122223333. Create the role in account 111122223333 with a trust policy that lets the EdgeRelay service principal assume it. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:iam::111122223333:role/edgerelay-exporter as the principal and allows PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on arn:objstore:::edge-request-logs/cdn/*, because large hourly files are uploaded in parts. This bucket policy statement is the only grant involved. In the EdgeRelay distribution settings, select the role, set the prefix to cdn/, and choose hourly partitioning by date. Wait for the next hour boundary and check that a directory named for the date and hour contains tab-separated log files. Incomplete uploads that remain visible in the bucket indicate that AbortMultipartUpload is missing from the statement.

This guide enables NetFlowLens to deliver virtual network flow records to a bucket named netflow-records. The bucket and the delivery role, netflowlens-delivery, are in account 111122223333. Create the role and set its trust policy to allow the NetFlowLens service principal. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on arn:objstore:::netflow-records/flows/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:objstore:::netflow-records. Do not edit the bucket policy; access within one account is granted through this identity-based policy. Configure the flow log to write Parquet files at ten-minute intervals with the key layout flows/vpc-id/date/. After twenty minutes, list the prefix and confirm that at least one Parquet file exists for each monitored network. Files of zero bytes suggest the monitored network had no traffic, not a permission problem.

This guide enables NetFlowLens to deliver virtual network flow records to a bucket named netflow-records. The bucket is in account 444455556666, and the delivery role, netflowlens-delivery, is in account 111122223333. Create the role in account 111122223333 and set its trust policy to allow the NetFlowLens service principal. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names the role ARN as the principal and allows PutObject on arn:objstore:::netflow-records/flows/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:objstore:::netflow-records. Access across the two accounts is granted through this bucket policy statement. Configure the flow log to write Parquet files at ten-minute intervals with the key layout flows/vpc-id/date/. After twenty minutes, list the prefix and confirm that at least one Parquet file exists for each monitored network. Files of zero bytes suggest the monitored network had no traffic, not a permission problem.

This guide configures ResolverTrace to store DNS query logs in a bucket named dns-query-logs. The bucket and the writer role, resolvertrace-writer, both belong to account 111122223333. Create the role with a trust policy for the ResolverTrace service principal. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on arn:objstore:::dns-query-logs/resolver/* and ListBucket on arn:objstore:::dns-query-logs, restricted to the resolver/ prefix with a prefix condition. The bucket policy is left untouched, and the identity-based policy supplies the whole grant. Associate the role with the query log configuration and set the output format to JSON lines. Run a test query against a hosted zone and wait for the next flush, which occurs every five minutes. Confirm that a file under resolver/ contains the query name, record type, and response code for the test query.

This guide exports slow query logs from a managed database named QueryLedger to a bucket named db-slowlog-export. The bucket and the export role, queryledger-export, are in account 111122223333. Create the role with a trust policy that allows the QueryLedger service principal to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on arn:objstore:::db-slowlog-export/slowlog/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:objstore:::db-slowlog-export. No bucket policy change is needed because the role and the bucket share an account. Set the instance parameter that logs statements slower than two seconds, and schedule the export every fifteen minutes. After one export cycle, read the newest object under slowlog/ and verify that it contains statement text, duration, and client host. If the export reports an authorization error, check that the role named in the export task is the one carrying the identity-based policy.

This guide exports slow query logs from a managed database named QueryLedger to a bucket named db-slowlog-export. The bucket is in account 444455556666, and the export role, queryledger-export, is in account 111122223333. Create the role in account 111122223333 with a trust policy that allows the QueryLedger service principal to assume it. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:iam::111122223333:role/queryledger-export as the principal and allows PutObject on arn:objstore:::db-slowlog-export/slowlog/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:objstore:::db-slowlog-export. The bucket policy change is required because the role and the bucket are in different accounts. Set the instance parameter that logs statements slower than two seconds, and schedule the export every fifteen minutes. After one export cycle, read the newest object under slowlog/ and verify that it contains statement text, duration, and client host. If the export reports an authorization error, check that the principal in the bucket policy matches the role named in the export task.

This guide configures the storage service's own server access logging, handled by BucketScribe, to write request records for a source bucket into a log bucket named storage-access-logs. The log bucket and the BucketScribe role, bucketscribe-delivery, are in account 111122223333. Create the role with a trust policy for the BucketScribe service principal. Attach an identity-based policy thatallows PutObject on arn:objstore:::storage-access-logs/source-logs/* only. The bucket policy of storage-access-logs is not changed, since the identity-based policy is the sole grant. Enable logging on the source bucket, choosing storage-access-logs as the target and source-logs/ as the prefix. Perform a few GET and PUT requests against the source bucket and wait about an hour for the first batch. Open one delivered file and confirm that it records the requester, operation, object key, and HTTP status.

This guide configures the storage service's own server access logging, handled by BucketScribe, to write request records for a source bucket into a log bucket named storage-access-logs. The log bucket belongs to account 444455556666, and the BucketScribe role, bucketscribe-delivery, belongs to account 111122223333. Create the role in account 111122223333 with a trust policy for the BucketScribe service principal. The owner of storage-access-logs adds a bucket policy statement naming the role ARN as the principal that allows PutObject on arn:objstore:::storage-access-logs/source-logs/* only. That bucket policy statement is the sole grant. Enable logging on the source bucket, choosing storage-access-logs as the target and source-logs/ as the prefix. Perform a few GET and PUT requests against the source bucket and wait about an hour for the first batch. Open one delivered file and confirm that it records the requester, operation, object key, and HTTP status.

This guide sets up RunLogStream to deliver container runtime logs to a bucket named runtime-log-store and lets a verification user read them back. The bucket, the delivery role runlogstream-shipper, and the user log-reviewer are all in account 111122223333. Create the role with a trust policy for the RunLogStream service principal. Attach an identity-based policy to the role allowing PutObject on arn:objstore:::runtime-log-store/containers/*, and attach one to log-reviewer allowing GetObject and ListBucket for the same prefix. Do not alter the bucket policy; both grants are made by identity-based policies in the same account. Configure each cluster to ship logs hourly into containers/cluster-name/date/. Once an hour has passed, sign in as log-reviewer and list the prefix to find the newest file. Download it and verify that every line has a pod name, a timestamp, and a message field.

This guide sets up RunLogStream to deliver container runtime logs to a bucket named runtime-log-store and lets a verification user read them back. The bucket belongs to account 444455556666, while the delivery role runlogstream-shipper and the user log-reviewer belong to account 111122223333. Create the role with a trust policy for the RunLogStream service principal. The bucket owner adds bucket policy statements that name the role ARN as the principal allowing PutObject on arn:objstore:::runtime-log-store/containers/*, and name the log-reviewer ARN as the principal allowing GetObject and ListBucket for the same prefix. Both grants are therefore made by the bucket policy in the owning account. Configure each cluster to ship logs hourly into containers/cluster-name/date/. Once an hour has passed, sign in as log-reviewer and list the prefix to find the newest file. Download it and verify that every line has a pod name, a timestamp, and a message field.
